assumptions: Customer impact is assumed to have begun at 00:00 UTC, when the error signature changed, rather than at 00:05 UTC when the alert fired; the alert lag is inferred from the metric window, not measured.
Who changed the flag and why is not recorded in the material reviewed; the change was treated as unintentional or at least unaccompanied by a rollout plan.

The absence of a deploy is taken from the change log being complete and accurate for the 24 hours before onset. An unrecorded code change landing at exactly 00:00 was considered and judged unsupported, but not formally excluded.
The divide-by-zero is assumed to sit in the non-legacy checkout path itself; this is inferred from the timing and the error signature, not from reading or bisecting the code.
Impact is assumed limited to the account page / checkout flow on io-shop, since no other surface appeared in the logs reviewed.

The steady low rate of UpstreamTimeout errors on the legacy path is pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident, and 'back at baseline' means a return to that pre-existing level rather than an error-free service.
Recovery was judged from the service's own metrics answering at baseline within the observation window; no independent check of customer-side success was performed.
input.executive_summary: Shortly after midnight UTC on 14 September, a configuration switch was turned off in the online shop, which sent customers down a newer checkout code path that contained a latent software defect. From 00:00 UTC, a substantial share of attempts to load the account page failed outright; customers on the affected path would have seen errors rather than their account and checkout details. Automated monitoring raised an alert at 00:05 UTC, an automated responder identified the configuration change as the cause within about twenty seconds, and the switch was put back to its previous setting. The service was confirmed back at its normal behaviour at 00:06 UTC, roughly one minute after the alert and about six minutes after customer impact began. The underlying defect in the newer checkout path has not been fixed — it is only hidden again by the restored setting, so re-enabling that path before the bug is repaired would reproduce the outage.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was switched from on to off at 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z, routing account-page traffic onto the non-legacy checkout code path, which contains an unguarded divide-by-zero: at that exact minute the error signature on io-shop changed from sporadic `UpstreamTimeout` to constant `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` and the error rate stepped up sharply. The fallback path had been masking the bug, so no deploy was needed to trigger it — the change log shows no production change in the preceding 24 hours.
